items.q: What does urllib.parse.quote('777 Valencia St, San Francisco') return?
rationales: quote_plus writes a plus for a space; quote writes %20, and it also encodes the comma.
quote does change the string: a space and a comma are percent-encoded.
Every value is a list, because a name may appear more than once.
That list of pairs is what parse_qsl returns, not parse_qs.
The .. goes up from /a/ to the root, so the a folder is left.

items.q: A robots.txt holds 'User-agent: *' and 'Disallow: /search*'. On Python 3.14.4, what does urllib.robotparser's can_fetch('*', 'https://pypi.org/search/?q=x') answer?
options: True, because the rule text is compared as a literal prefix and the path does not start with the characters /search*
It raises an error for the wildcard
rationales: RFC 9309 reads * as a wildcard, but the standard-library parser was run and answered True.
No error is raised; the line is read and compared as plain text.
403 is Forbidden.
Not a phrase of the standard.

items.q: A page holds tu. What does re.findall(r'', page) return?
rationales: The first tag has a class before the href, so the pattern does not match it.
Only the second tag matches the pattern.

items.q:
A standard-library HTMLParser is fed '

a <b> c

' with its default settings. What does handle_data receive?
rationales: That is what convert_charrefs=False gives.
The references are converted to characters by default.

items.q: With Beautiful Soup, what do select('#zz') and select_one('#zz') return when nothing has the id zz?
options: An error is raised by both
rationales: select returns an empty list, not None.
Neither raises; Selenium's find_element is the one that raises.

items.q: The temperature in an OpenWeather answer is 285.44 and the chapter uses the default units. What is it in Celsius, to one decimal?
rationales: The value is in Kelvin; 273.15 must be subtracted.
Adding 273.15 goes the wrong way.

items.q: Which statement about Selenium's find_element and find_elements is correct?
options: find_element returns the first match and raises NoSuchElementException when there is none; find_elements gives an empty list
Both return None when nothing matches
find_elements raises NoSuchElementException and find_element returns an empty list
rationales: The chapter and the documentation say find_element raises.
The two are the other way round.

items.q: searchpypi.py opens min(5, len(link_elems)) tabs. How many for 0, 3 and 12 links?
rationales: min picks the smaller number, so fewer links open fewer tabs.
The cap of 5 still applies to 12 links.

items.q: A page builds its content with JavaScript after it loads. What does the chapter say about downloading it with requests?
options: requests runs the scripts, so the content is there
The downloaded text lacks that content, so a browser driver is needed unless the site offers an API
Beautiful Soup runs the scripts when it parses the text
rationales: requests only downloads text.
A parser does not run scripts.
